judged_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic background job, which re-downloads and re-imports the entire RSS feed on every embed miss. One anonymous page view of a not-yet-imported article triggers a full-feed fetch plus N TopicEmbed lookups/imports; a popular blog page with no topic yet turns each 60-second throttle window into a full-feed poll, hammering the publisher's server and the Discourse DB from web traffic; the shape should be an enqueue plus a targeted fetch, not a synchronous full poll per request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` synchronously calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `TopicRetriever` is invoked from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` background job (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), which is enqueued on an embed miss (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` downloads and parses the entire feed and iterates all items (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then `rss.items.each`), potentially doing many `TopicEmbed.import` operations per miss. This is a diff-grounded architectural/performance concern (on-demand full-feed polling triggered by embed misses), not a direct correctness/security defect.
